t: You're looking at the London Palladium, a Grade II star listed West End theatre on Argyll Street in Soho. Frank Matcham designed it, and it opened in 1910. It seats 2,286 people. Matcham designed over ninety theatres in his career. Walter Gibbons, a theatre proprietor who led the employers' side in the 1907 Music Hall Strike, owned it. On 13 October 1963, the Beatles played Sunday Night at the London Palladium, and a newspaper coined the word Beatlemania. Bruce Forsyth is buried here.
